title: Ang 659: Bhikhan
tomorrow: the groom is scared at 5 a.m. who's he supposed to tell?

segments.voice: Yesterday, the bhagats: Ravidas binding God with love, a lover's dare or a beggar's grip. One more bhagat closes Sorath today, and he's tired.

Cough syrup tastes like a dare. Ginger tea burns on the way down. Plain water, when you're really sick, can taste like the best thing in the world. On ang 659, the bhagat Bhikhan answers yesterday's question. His body is giving out, and the medicine he asks for is the Name, which he pictures as pure, sweet water.
screen: `SYRUP, GINGER, PLAIN WATER.` → `A BODY GIVING OUT.` → `THE NAME AS WATER.`

segments.voice: Bhikhan's hymns in Sorath close the raga. The first is honest about old age, in paraphrase: my eyes run with water, my body has grown weak, my hair has turned white as milk. My throat is choked; I can't get a word out. What can a person do now? Then he turns. O Lord, be my physician, and save your devotee. Notice he doesn't pretend. The list is plain and physical: eyes, hair, throat. He doesn't call the body unimportant. He describes it failing, in detail, and then asks for help from the one he trusts. And the help has a taste. Bhikhan calls the Lord's Name pure, nectar-like water, the medicine, by the Guru's grace. Medicine is something you take in, a little at a time, not something you think about. Here's what the hymn doesn't say. It never tells anyone to skip a doctor or stop caring for the body. It asks God to be the physician of the whole person, the one who stays when the voice gives out. And it's worth noticing: one of the last voices in raga Sorath is an old man who can barely speak, and his hymn is kept in the Granth for everyone to sing.
screen: `EYES, HAIR, THROAT: HONEST AGE.` · `BE MY PHYSICIAN.` · `THE NAME AS PURE WATER.` · `IT NEVER SAYS SKIP THE DOCTOR.` · then, large: `MEDICINE.`

segments.voice: Pour a small glass of plain water. Take one slow sip and hold it in your mouth a moment before you swallow, noticing its cool, its taste, the way it goes down. Sip again, slowly, a few times through the sit, as if it were medicine.
Ang 659. Where the bhagat Bhikhan closes Sorath: an old body giving out, and the Name as pure water, the medicine.
Hold onto this: medicine, taken a sip at a time, the way Sorath ends, with a glass of water. Rest well.

howItsDone: Bhikhan's hymns are read with the other bhagats' at the end of raga Sorath in the Guru Granth Sahib; Sikhs often speak of the Name as a medicine, a healing for the whole person.
